concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: Linear-time XOR/addition of the bit at a common offset of several address chunks on rectangle or grouped-stream layouts, used to change selected address bits; exceptional addresses are repaired by sorting.

concepts.name: Schoolbook multiplication and divide and conquer
concepts.gloss: Ordinary digit-by-digit multiplication takes O(n^2) bit operations, and divide-and-conquer recursions split a problem into smaller subproblems whose costs are summed.

concepts.name: Recurrences and geometric sums
concepts.gloss: Running times of recursive procedures are bounded by solving recurrences and summing geometric series.

concepts.name: Logarithms, floors and ceilings
concepts.gloss: Base-2 logarithms and the floor and ceiling functions are used to describe sizes, bit lengths and number of levels.

concepts.name: Binary representation and bitwise operations
concepts.gloss: Integers are written as strings of bits in base 2 (or any radix), and XOR is bitwise addition modulo 2.

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on integers reduced modulo a positive integer, including addition, multiplication and inverses of units.

concepts.name: Divisibility, primes and coprimality
concepts.gloss: Divisibility, prime numbers and the greatest common divisor, with integers being coprime when their gcd is 1.

concepts.name: Permutations and sorting
concepts.gloss: A permutation is a bijective rearrangement of a finite list, and sorting is an algorithm that reorders items into a given order.

concepts.name: Linear algebra over a field
concepts.gloss: Matrices and linear maps on vector spaces, with notions of invertibility, rank, subspaces, dimension and bases.

concepts.name: Triangular matrices and elementary operations
concepts.gloss: Triangular matrices have zeros on one side of the diagonal, and Gaussian elimination reduces matrices using elementary row operations.

concepts.name: The field with two elements
concepts.gloss: The field of residues modulo 2, in which addition is XOR and multiplication is AND.

concepts.name: Rational numbers and dyadic fractions
concepts.gloss: Rational numbers are ratios of integers, and dyadic rationals are those with a power-of-two denominator, i.e. finite binary fractions.

concepts.name: Rounding and approximation error
concepts.gloss: Real values are rounded or truncated to a fixed precision, and errors are bounded using absolute values and the triangle inequality.

concepts.name: Cyclic groups and powers of a generator
concepts.gloss: The integers modulo n under addition form a cyclic group, and indices of arrays are often treated as elements of such groups.

concepts.name: Array indexing by tuples and mixed radix
concepts.gloss: An array can be indexed by tuples of digits, stored in lexicographic order on a tape, with the tuple read as a mixed-radix number.

concepts.name: Sums, products and indicator notation
concepts.gloss: Standard notation for sums, products and indicators of conditions.

concepts.name: Basic complexity of tape computation
concepts.gloss: A deterministic machine can copy, scan or compare tape contents in time linear in their length, and subroutines can be composed by adding their costs.

concepts.name: Euclidean norm and inequalities
concepts.gloss: The size of a number or vector is measured by its norm, and a map is contractive if it does not increase norm.

concepts.name: Gaussian integers
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers a+bi with integer a and b, which add and multiply like integers with i^2 = -1.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science background: asymptotic analysis and recurrences, discrete mathematics (modular arithmetic, primes, gcd, permutations, binary representation), introductory linear algebra (matrices, rank, invertibility, vector spaces), and basic algebra with polynomials and complex numbers. They know algorithms such as schoolbook multiplication, divide and conquer and sorting, and basic Turing machines with tapes. They have not studied the FFT or Schönhage–Strassen in depth, rings and finite fields beyond basics, tensor products, or the specialist multitape-complexity and fast-multiplication literature.
